data.narrative:
Aalo Atomics is a Series B-stage nuclear energy company that has raised $300M+ to date. The broader nuclear energy sector includes 3 public comparables (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private peers, among them Valar Atomics, Helion, Oklo, X-Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy. A sufficiently narrow peer set—controlling for stage, valuation tier, and business model maturity—is not available; the sector contains only 1 same-stage comparable and 1 adjacent-stage peer, falling short of the 3-datapoint threshold for robust peer-median analysis.

Given data constraints, stage-progression methodology is the applicable triangulation approach. Using total raised ($300M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B to subsequent-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $570M. This single-method result establishes a median point; sensitivity around execution risk and sector-specific capital intensity suggests a reasonable range of $484M (low) to $656M (high).

The analysis supports a valuation band centered at $570M, though confidence is constrained by the absence of sufficiently granular peer comparables in early-stage nuclear. Key uncertainties include technology differentiation within the crowded frontier-nuclear landscape, path to commercialization timelines, and whether capital-intensity economics will track historical nuclear precedent or diverge materially. Peer benchmarking as additional Series B or Series C rounds close in the sector would materially improve precision.
